title: Convoy
anecdote: The most massive anthem of rebellion of the 70s wasn't born in a hippie commune... but in a sliced bread commercial. William Fries created the fictional trucker C.W. McCall to sell bread on local Nebraska television. The commercials went viral, prompting Fries and composer Chip Davis to record actual songs under that alias. In 1975, the 55 mph national speed limit made CB radios explode in popularity among truckers. Inspired by that outlaw jargon, Fries wrote 'Convoy', a rebel caravan breaking through barriers. It sold millions of copies, fueled a global CB radio craze, and conquered the top of Billboard. Its success was so wild that director Sam Peckinpah brought it to the big screen. What outlaw route have you driven today?
